descriptors.evidence: numeric_parseable_fraction=1.0, 72 distinct values from a 150-row slice (uniqueness 0.48), samples 101-105 sequential. Co-occurring with a separate cold_cranking_amps field (the standard battery CCA spec) implies this amperage figure belongs to a different electrical part, most plausibly alternator output rating (typical real-world alternators run ~90-250A), though I cannot rule out another current-rated component from name+samples alone.

Only 4 distinct values (H11, H4, H7, 9005) with very low uniqueness (0.0267) matching standard halogen automotive bulb base/socket codes; numeric_parseable_fraction=0.26 reflects that '9005' parses as a number while H-codes do not. These exact codes are extremely common shopper search terms for headlight/fog bulbs.

Field name is the standard automotive battery spec name; numeric_parseable_fraction=1.0, high uniqueness (0.8733, 131 distinct of 150) consistent with a fine-grained per-battery-model spec rather than a coarse category. Shoppers commonly filter/search batteries by minimum CCA.

Only 2 distinct string values (Cylindrical, Panel), numeric_parseable_fraction=0.0, describing the physical form factor of an air/oil filter. Plausible but secondary shopper vocabulary ('panel filter', 'cone/cylindrical filter') compared to searching by vehicle fitment, so I temper confidence on retrieval usage despite confidence in the field's identity.

Samples (24F, 35, 65) match standard BCI automotive battery group-size codes exactly. numeric_parseable_fraction=0.66 confirms mixed alphanumeric codes (24F fails numeric parse, 35/65 succeed), a signature of this spec. Group size is a well-known, heavily-searched battery fitment facet on retail sites.

Values 4-8 (5 distinct, numeric_parseable_fraction=1.0, mean_value_length=1.0) match the small-integer heat-range numbering used by spark plug makers (NGK/Denso, typically ranging roughly 2-12). This is a genuine typed spec, but mainstream shoppers usually match spark plugs by vehicle/OEM part rather than typing a raw heat-range number, so I treat it as more useful for compatibility/ranking than as a primary retrieval facet.

numeric_parseable_fraction=1.0 with high uniqueness (0.94, 141 distinct of 150) and sample values in the 1000-1050 range consistent with per-bulb lumen output ratings. Lumens is a standard, frequently-searched lighting spec ('6000 lumen bulb').

Only 2 distinct values (Aluminum, Copper-Brass), numeric_parseable_fraction=0.0, mean_value_length=9.76 (compound term 'Copper-Brass' pulls the average up). Reads like a radiator/heat-exchanger construction material field; shoppers do sometimes filter cooling parts by material.

Sample values (Ceramic, Organic, Semi-Metallic) are the exact standard brake-pad friction material categories; numeric_parseable_fraction=0.0 and only 3 distinct values fit a closed material taxonomy. This is one of the most commonly searched brake-pad facets in real commerce.

numeric_parseable_fraction=1.0, 31 distinct values (10-14 shown, uniqueness 0.2067) consistent with filtration-fineness ratings for oil/air/fuel filters. Legitimate typed spec, but I judge it more of a secondary/enthusiast filter than a mainstream shopper query term, hence ranking_only rather than a primary retrieval facet.

Exactly 2 distinct values (Aftermarket, OEM) present across the full 1500-row catalog (occurrences=1500, unlike the 150-row category-specific specs), uniqueness=0.0013 — a global, low-cardinality classification. 'OEM vs aftermarket' is a very common shopper filter/search term in this vertical; modeled as enum rather than boolean since the two labels are named categories, not a true/false flag.

uniqueness_ratio=0.998 (1497 distinct of 1500 occurrences) is the classic signature of a per-item identifier, and variant_scoped=true confirms it is assigned at the specific variant level rather than shared across a product's variants — consistent with a real per-SKU part number (e.g. 'AM-1026-CB' differs from 'AM-1037-SP'). Shoppers frequently search by exact part number for cross-referencing.

2 distinct values (Front, Rear), uniqueness=0.0067, numeric_parseable_fraction=0.0 — a textbook installation-position enum for parts like brake pads/shocks that come in front/rear variants. occurrences=300 (double the 150 seen on most category specs) suggests it spans two sub-lines (e.g. front-set and rear-set SKUs) within the same product family. Extremely common shopper query modifier ('front brake pads').

Generic field name gives little direct signal. numeric_parseable_fraction=1.0, 13 distinct values, samples 16-20 (mean_value_length=2.0) form a sequential small-integer range that best matches common wiper-blade lengths in inches (typical retail range ~16"-28"), which is also a heavily-searched shopper facet ('22 inch wiper blade'). This is a genuine best guess, not a confident identification — the bare name 'size' could plausibly denote a different dimension (e.g. wheel or connector size) in a fuller catalog, so confidence is capped.

Samples (10mm, 12mm, 14mm) are a small closed set (3 distinct, uniqueness=0.02) of metric thread diameters, plausibly for oil drain plugs, spark plugs, or lug studs. numeric_parseable_fraction=0.0 because of the trailing 'mm' unit — the raw values are not directly numeric even though the underlying quantity is a measurement; after unit-stripping this could equally be modeled as a numeric_range. Fitment-critical and occasionally searched directly (e.g. 'm12 drain plug').

distinct_values=1 (only '12' observed, uniqueness=0.0067) shows zero variance in this particular sample, but that reflects this catalog slice being dominated by standard 12V automotive electrical parts, not that the field is meaningless — it is still a genuine, correctly-typed numeric spec (numeric_parseable_fraction=1.0) that would show real variance across a broader catalog (6V, 24V systems etc.), and '12v' is a common shopper qualifier.

Values 12/24/36/60 map cleanly to 1/2/3/5-year warranty terms (numeric_parseable_fraction=1.0, only 4 distinct of 1500 occurrences, uniqueness=0.0027 — a global attribute like oem_or_aftermarket rather than a category-specific spec). variant_scoped=true indicates warranty length was actually observed varying per-variant in this source, which is somewhat unusual (warranty is often product-level) but is what the data shows. Warranty length is a real, if secondary, shopper filter facet.
